title: Good coresolutions of complexes compute product totalization
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $M^\bullet,E_0^\bullet,E_1^\bullet,\ldots$ be integer-indexed cochain complexes of abelian groups, with differentials $d$ of degree $1$ satisfying $d^2=0$. Let $u:M^\bullet\to E_0^\bullet$ and $f_i:E_i^\bullet\to E_{i+1}^\bullet$ be chain maps. Assume $0\to M^\bullet\xrightarrow{u}E_0^\bullet\xrightarrow{f_0}E_1^\bullet\to\cdots$ is exact in every degree. Assume also that for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ the induced sequence $0\to M^n/d_M(M^{n-1})\to E_0^n/d_{E_0}(E_0^{n-1})\to E_1^n/d_{E_1}(E_1^{n-1})\to\cdots$ is exact. Define $T^n=\prod_{i\ge0}E_i^{n-i}$ and $(d_Tx)_i=f_{i-1}(x_{i-1})+(-1)^i d_{E_i}(x_i)$, with the first summand zero for $i=0$. Then the augmentation $M^\bullet\to T^\bullet$, $m\mapsto(u(m),0,0,\ldots)$, is a quasi-isomorphism, meaning that it induces isomorphisms on $H^n=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ for every $n$. No boundedness assumption on the individual complexes is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09J0, homology.tex, lemma-good-right-resolution-gives-qis, statement and the displayed product-total differential in its proof.

proof.text: Write $a:M^\bullet\to T^\bullet$ for the augmentation. Degreewise exactness gives $f_0u=0$ and $f_if_{i-1}=0$. For $i\ge1$, the $i$th component of $d_T^2x$ is $f_{i-1}f_{i-2}x_{i-2}+((-1)^{i-1}+(-1)^i)f_{i-1}d x_{i-1}+d^2x_i=0$, omitting the first term for $i=1$; the component $i=0$ is $d^2x_0=0$. We used $df_{i-1}=f_{i-1}d$. Similarly $d_Ta(m)=a(d_Mm)$, so this is a complex and $a$ is a chain map. All formulas use only finitely many coordinates at a time.

Apply [lem-sfb-good-coresolution-cohomology-rows] to the given chain maps: its degreewise exactness and differential-cokernel exactness are precisely the two assumptions of the item. Thus $0\to H^q(M)\to H^q(E_0)\to H^q(E_1)\to\cdots$ is exact for every $q$. This is the sole supporting theorem needed in the induction below.

Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$ and a cocycle $x=(x_i)\in T^n$. The first two cocycle equations give $d x_0=0$ and $f_0x_0=d x_1$. Exactness of the differential-cokernel row in degree $n$ gives $m\in M^n$ and $v\in E_0^{n-1}$ with $x_0=u(m)+dv$. Applying $d$ gives $u(dm)=0$, hence $dm=0$ since $u$ is degreewise injective. Replace $x$ by $r=x-a(m)$: it is a cocycle with $r_0=dv$. It remains to construct $y\in T^{n-1}$ with $d_Ty=r$. Start with $y_0=v$, which solves the coordinate-zero equation.

Inductively suppose $y_0,\ldots,y_k$, with $y_j\in E_j^{n-j-1}$, solve $r_j=f_{j-1}y_{j-1}+(-1)^jdy_j$ for $0\le j\le k$ (omit $f_{-1}y_{-1}$). Put $w=r_{k+1}-f_ky_k\in E_{k+1}^{n-k-1}$. The cocycle equation for $r$ gives $dr_{k+1}=(-1)^k f_kr_k$, so $dw=0$ by the equation at $k$ and $f_kf_{k-1}=0$. Also $f_{k+1}w=f_{k+1}r_{k+1}=(-1)^{k+3}dr_{k+2}$ is a boundary. By [lem-sfb-good-coresolution-cohomology-rows] in degree $n-k-1$, choose a cycle $z\in E_k^{n-k-1}$ whose image under $f_k$ has cohomology class $[w]$. Replace $y_k$ by $y_k+z$. This keeps its equation because $dz=0$; it leaves all earlier equations unchanged. Now $w-f_kz$ is a boundary, so choose $y_{k+1}\in E_{k+1}^{n-k-2}$ with $(-1)^{k+1}dy_{k+1}=w-f_kz$. This solves the next coordinate equation and completes the induction.

Choose witnesses recursively in the preceding construction. At stage $k+1$ only $y_k$ is changed and $y_{k+1}$ is added. Each coordinate $y_j$ is therefore fixed permanently after stage $j+1$; take this final value as the $j$th coordinate of $y\in\prod_{j\ge0}E_j^{n-j-1}=T^{n-1}$. The equation at coordinate $j$ holds once the coordinates $j-1,j$ have stabilized, so it holds for this $y$. Hence $d_Ty=r$, and $[x]=H^n(a)[m]$. This proves surjectivity. No limit in a topological group or infinite sum is involved: $y$ is simply the family of its final coordinates.

For injectivity, let $m\in M^n$ be a cocycle and suppose $a(m)=d_Ty$ for $y\in T^{n-1}$. Coordinates zero and one say $u(m)=dy_0$ and $f_0y_0=dy_1$. Thus the class of $y_0$ in $E_0^{n-1}/d(E_0^{n-2})$ lies in the kernel of the map to $E_1^{n-1}/d(E_1^{n-2})$. The assumed exact cokernel row in degree $n-1$ gives $z\in M^{n-1}$ and $t\in E_0^{n-2}$ with $y_0=u(z)+dt$. Differentiating yields $u(m)=u(dz)$; degreewise injectivity of $u$ gives $m=dz$. Therefore $H^n(a)$ is injective. Together with surjectivity, for arbitrary $n$, this proves the stated quasi-isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem augmentation_quasiIso (M : CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u} ℤ) (E : ℕ → CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u} ℤ) (u : M ⟶ E 0) (f : ∀ i : ℕ, E i ⟶ E (i + 1)) (h_inj : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Injective (u.f n)) (h₀ : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Exact (u.f n) ((f 0).f n)) (h : ∀ (i : ℕ) (n : ℤ), Function.Exact ((f i).f n) ((f (i + 1)).f n)) (hc_inj : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Injective (opcyclesMap u n)) (hc₀ : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Exact (opcyclesMap u n) (opcyclesMap (f 0) n)) (hc : ∀ (i : ℕ) (n : ℤ), Function.Exact (opcyclesMap (f i) n) (opcyclesMap (f (i + 1)) n)) : QuasiIso (augmentation M E u f h h₀)
